title: Fever After Kasai
code: BARD Delphi 2022 · expert opinion · no society treatment guideline

blocks.text:
**After a Kasai, any of: fever, paler stools, new or deeper jaundice, or a rising bilirubin or GGT:** think cholangitis — assess now, blood culture, low threshold for IV antibiotics and admission. Fever is not required.
**Shock, lethargy, poor perfusion or apnea:** sepsis — resuscitate, culture, broad IV antibiotics now; check INR and glucose. Ill young infant: consider a lumbar puncture.
**Bleeding:** INR and vitamin K; GI bleeding may be variceal.
**On oral prophylaxis:** prophylaxis does not exclude cholangitis — treat it, with a different class.
**Recurrent episodes, multiple bile lakes, or bilirubin that does not come back down:** call the transplant center.

groups.label: Before the first dose
items: Blood culture — 2 sets if possible; line culture if a central line

groups.label: Blood — today
items: Total and conjugated bilirubin, GGT, ALT, AST, albumin

groups.label: Imaging
items: Abdominal ultrasound with Doppler within 24 h: bile lakes, ascites, portal flow, other source

groups.label: Start now
items: IV antibiotics after the culture — choice by local antibiogram; dose with pharmacy
Feeds back as soon as stable — NG if oral intake is poor
Ask: date of Kasai, stool color trend, prophylaxis agent, past episodes and cultures
Cholangitis without fever — only 41% of physician-diagnosed episodes had fever or shivering; GGT or bilirubin was raised or rising in 90% (Madadi-Sanjani 2024)
Kasai failure behind the infection — bilirubin that does not come back down after treatment needs transplant referral
Bile lakes or a liver abscess — repeat the ultrasound when fever persists
Line sepsis and UTI — the other common sources
Meningitis — in an ill-appearing young infant, consider a lumbar puncture
Vitamin K deficiency — check INR before lines, drains or biopsy
Hypoglycemia when feeds stop — small glycogen reserve

blocks.text:
After a Kasai, bile drains through a Roux loop of bowel into a scarred, poorly draining biliary tree. Bacteria reach it easily and clear slowly. Antireflux valves and long conduits did not prevent this (lesson 03-05).

Cholangitis is the most common complication after the Kasai. In 223 US infants, 57% had at least one episode in the first year (Kelley-Quon 2022). In a Korean series the cumulative incidence was 76% at 1 year, and cholangitis recurred in 76% (Baek 2020). Reported rates vary widely, mostly because definitions differ.

It often looks mild. In 59 children with cholangitis in the first year, only 41% had fever or shivering, but GGT or bilirubin was raised or rising in 90%. Blood cultures were positive in 1 of 59 (Madadi-Sanjani 2024). So treat on criteria, not on the culture.

The organisms are gut flora. In Korea, Enterococcus faecium led (28%), then E. coli, Enterobacter cloacae and Klebsiella. Only 38% of gram-negatives were cefotaxime-susceptible (Baek 2020, single center). This is why many centers start with piperacillin–tazobactam or a carbapenem rather than ceftriaxone.

Each episode can stop bile flow. Recurrent cholangitis predicts loss of the native liver and is an indication for transplant referral (lessons 03-07, 03-08, 03-12).

items.text: "No fever, so not cholangitis." Paler stools or a rising GGT may be the only sign.
"Culture negative, so viral." Cultures are often negative; treat on the BARD criteria.
"The Kasai has failed." Treat the cholangitis first, then judge drainage.
"She is on prophylaxis." Breakthrough is common — treat it, and use a different class.
"Oral after 3 days." Consensus durations are 10–14 days (suspected) and 14–21 days (confirmed); no data support an early oral switch (lesson 03-07).

Ceftriaxone (FDA label): contraindicated in hyperbilirubinemic neonates, in preterm infants up to 41 weeks postmenstrual age, and in neonates ≤ 28 days who need IV calcium, including PN. It also causes gallbladder pseudolithiasis — a trap on the next ultrasound.
TMP-SMX is contraindicated under 2 months of age and in marked hepatic damage (FDA label) — relevant when choosing prophylaxis.
Teen or adult after a Kasai: ERCP usually cannot reach the ducts through the Roux loop. Use antibiotics, MRCP and IR drainage (lesson 03-13).
Teach every family: pale stools or fever — call the same day.

rows.topic: Definition of cholangitis after the Kasai

positions.bard_delphi_2022: Suspected: 1 clinical + 1 lab/imaging criterion. Confirmed: 2 + 2, or suspected plus a positive blood culture
positions.madadi_sanjani_2024_bard: Retrospective check: very strong correlation with clinicians' diagnosis (r = 0.8), but 15 of 59 clinical diagnoses (25%) did not meet the criteria

rows.note: No society guideline. The Delphi is expert consensus for the first year after the Kasai; prospective validation is ongoing. Adult Tokyo criteria do not fit infants.
Expert consensus only; no trial compares durations for cholangitis. The lessons used these durations as standard.

positions.bard_delphi_2022: No agent recommended; piperacillin–tazobactam most used (71% of survey respondents)
positions.wang_2023_cholangitis_rct: Febrile cholangitis graded by the trial's own scale. Mild: cefoperazone–tazobactam no worse than meropenem; severe: meropenem, IVIG shortened fever (one open-label trial, China)

rows.note: No guideline. Choose by local resistance; cefoperazone is not available in the US.

positions.bard_delphi_2022: Give for 6–12 months; agent not specified
positions.chen_2026_prophylaxis_meta: Cholangitis 56.9% vs 56.6% with and without (OR 0.88, 95% CI 0.41–1.92); native-liver survival higher with prophylaxis in a subset of studies (54% vs 36%)

rows.note: Consensus practice versus null meta-analyses of weak studies; the survival signal comes from few studies. The North American transplant-evaluation guideline (AASLD/AST/NASPGHAN, 2014; updated 2026) is reported to support prophylaxis — pending its full text, so this verdict is provisional. The app treats prophylaxis as optional: one agent, a written stop date, and never a reason to skip cultures.
